_comment: Frozen dispatch cases. `expected` is the single canonical answer and drives the
confusion matrix; `acceptable` is the set scored as correct, and is wider than
`expected` only where two skills genuinely share a boundary.
These expectations are a specification, not ground truth handed down from
anywhere. The first live run calibrates them: a disagreement on run one is as
likely to be a wrong expectation as a wrong dispatch, and should be adjudicated
by hand. Every run after that is drift detection against a set already argued
over. Editing a case AFTER seeing a run fail it is how a regression suite stops
measuring anything -- record the reason in the repo when it happens.
`guards` names a manual-only skill (disable-model-invocation: true) that a
negative case protects. It counts as coverage for that skill and nothing else;

cases.prompt: https://www.carvana.com/vehicle/2861049 thoughts?
cases.why: Bare 'thoughts?' beside a listing URL. The description claims this exact phrasing.

cases.prompt: 2023 Volvo XC40 Recharge, 31k miles, $28,400. Grade this.
cases.why: Named year/make/model with price and an explicit grade request.

cases.prompt: What's the actual difference between a Volvo XC40 Recharge and a C40 Recharge?
cases.why: Names a specific model but attaches no purchase decision. The description's explicit non-trigger.

cases.prompt: Why do electric cars lose so much range in cold weather?
cases.why: General automotive trivia. Should not fire.

cases.prompt: retro this session
cases.why: Verbatim trigger phrase from the description.

cases.prompt: How could we have done that faster and with less back and forth?
cases.why: Paraphrase of a claimed trigger, never using the word 'audit'.

cases.prompt: Debrief the Anthropic interview I just finished.
cases.why: improvement-notes explicitly disclaims interview debriefs. The postmortem skill that owns them is project-scoped to resume_project and is not installed globally, so from the home directory either interview-loop or no skill is defensible. improvement-notes is the failure.
A bare case number with no other context. The description claims this.

cases.prompt: build me a jira ticket for 268386
cases.why: Unambiguous. If this one ever fails, the skill is broken outright.

cases.prompt: is 00268386 even an engineering ticket?
cases.why: The description claims this phrasing specifically.

cases.prompt: How many cases did the team close last week?
cases.why: Case-shaped and Salesforce-shaped, but it is a reporting question the sf-caseops MCP tools answer directly. jira-ticket-builder states no non-trigger boundary, so this is the case most likely to over-fire.

cases.prompt: run the baseline against Opus 5.2
cases.why: Verbatim trigger.

cases.prompt: Test the new model when it drops.
cases.why: The description claims this without the word 'baseline' appearing.

cases.prompt: Is Opus 5 actually better than Sonnet 5 for long-form writing?
cases.why: Model comparison as opinion, not a request to run anything. model-baseline states no non-trigger boundary, so this is where it would over-fire.

cases.prompt: What interviews do I have coming up?
cases.why: Verbatim trigger.

cases.prompt: prep me for Baseten
cases.why: The description claims 'prep me for [company]'.

cases.prompt: Put 30 minutes on my calendar tomorrow afternoon.
cases.why: Calendar-shaped and adjacent to interview-loop's data sources, but it is a scheduling request with no interview in it.

cases.prompt: What's the weather in Atlanta this weekend?
cases.why: Control. Any skill firing here means dispatch is over-eager across the board.

cases.prompt: Write me a Python function that reverses a string in place.
cases.why: Control. Ordinary coding request.

cases.prompt: skill check
cases.why: Bare verbatim trigger, two words, no other context.

cases.prompt: Did any of my skills break?
cases.why: Paraphrase of a claimed trigger without the word 'skill check'.

cases.prompt: Run the baseline against Opus 5.2 and tell me how it scores.
cases.why: The nearest neighbour. skill-check disclaims the frozen model-quality suite explicitly; this must reach model-baseline, not skill-check. Guards against the new skill stealing its prompts.

cases.prompt: Find me some new Claude skills worth installing.
cases.why: Skill-shaped but it is discovery, not health. skill-check disclaims it; the weekly skill scan owns it and is a scheduled task, not a dispatchable skill.

cases.prompt: Did the Opus 5.2 upgrade break any of my skills?
cases.why: The description claims 'whether a model upgrade broke his skills'. The model name is model-baseline's hook, so this is the prompt most likely to be stolen.

cases.prompt: That skill check took forever. How could we have run it faster?
cases.why: Says 'skill check' verbatim but asks for an audit of the session, which skill-check explicitly hands to improvement-notes. skill-check firing is the failure.

cases.prompt: I want to turn the sunny corner by the mailbox into a native pollinator bed, roughly 12 by 8. Plan it out.
cases.why: Clear positive: a new perennial bed with dimensions and a request to plan it.

cases.prompt: same deliverable as the half-moon, but for the strip along the driveway
cases.why: Verbatim trigger phrase from the description, with no plant or bed vocabulary beyond 'strip'.

cases.prompt: Prairie Moon has these 9-plant pollinator power packs. How would I lay a few of them out along a 20 ft fence?
cases.why: Kit-shopping paraphrase the description claims; never says 'plan' or 'design'.

cases.prompt: Plan my raised vegetable beds for spring: tomatoes, peppers, and squash.
cases.why: Near-miss the description disclaims: bed planning, but annual vegetables. diy-home-context firing here scores as outside tested set, not a miss.

cases.prompt: What's the cheapest way to buy everything for both beds this fall? I'd rather not place six different orders.
cases.why: The order-optimizer trigger: a shopping question with no bed-design vocabulary, which only makes sense with the skill's plans and price catalog.

cases.prompt: The stone steps down to the meadow shift after every rain. How do I stabilize them?
cases.why: Hardscape and drainage, both handed to diy-home-context by name in the description. 'Meadow' is the bait.

cases.prompt: Will swamp milkweed survive in Atlanta clay?
cases.why: A question about one plant, which the description disclaims. Native-plant vocabulary with no bed attached.

cases.prompt: Take another pass at the half-moon meadow plan and swap the bluestar for something that blooms in August.
cases.why: The revision trigger ('a second pass or revision of an existing plan'), which no other case exercises.

cases.prompt: Spec a flow for reassigning a case back to the queue when the owner has been offline for an hour.
cases.why: Verbatim 'spec a flow for'.

cases.prompt: When a case gets created from email, I want Priority set from the account tier. Would this be before-save or after-save?
cases.why: The description claims this question specifically.

cases.prompt: Why didn't the first-response milestone flow fire on case 00268386?
cases.why: Debugging an existing flow on a real case, not designing one. flow-spec-builder states no non-trigger boundary and the case number is jira-ticket-builder's bait, so this catches over-firing from both. salesforce-iapartments firing scores as outside tested set.

cases.prompt: Case 00268386 needs the reopen flow fixed. Build me the Jira ticket for it.
cases.why: Flow vocabulary plus an explicit ticket request. jira-ticket-builder owns it; flow-spec-builder is the failure.

cases.prompt: I'm creating #sleep, make it for sleep tracking
cases.why: The claimed 'I'm creating #fitness' phrasing with a new channel name, so it tests the pattern rather than a memorized string.

cases.prompt: The PhoneLog bot has gone quiet in #fitness and pings are coming through iMessage instead. What broke?
cases.why: The troubleshooting trigger ('bot silent, pings falling back to iMessage'). No case in this group asks for a send: MCP tools are not on the dispatch denylist.

cases.prompt: How do I get a Discord bot to reply inside a thread instead of the channel?
cases.why: The description's own non-trigger: a one-off Discord API question unrelated to PhoneLog.

cases.prompt: ship sunday
cases.why: Bare verbatim trigger.

cases.prompt: Run the weekly increment on the portfolio.
cases.why: Paraphrase of 'run the weekly increment'.

cases.prompt: Turn on GitHub Pages for my deflection-audit repo.
cases.why: The exact gh step ship-sunday performs mid-run, asked as a one-off. No non-trigger boundary in the description, and a false fire here starts a public increment.

cases.prompt: I'm about to build a small web app that tracks my garden plantings. What stack should I use, and are there similar projects I should look at first?
cases.why: Stack selection plus comparables, both claimed. The garden vocabulary is bait for garden-bed-build.

cases.prompt: Look over the skill-regression-harness repo and tell me what you'd change about its architecture.
cases.why: Repo analysis and architecture critique, both claimed. The repo name is bait for skill-check.

cases.prompt: This test fails with KeyError: 'expected' on line 212. What's wrong?
cases.why: The narrow single-bug debugging the description says to avoid.

cases.prompt: Audit this README for AI tells before I push it.
cases.why: 'Audit a README' is claimed. No README is attached, so the decision rests on intent alone.

cases.prompt: Does this sound like ChatGPT wrote it? "In today's fast-paced landscape, it's worth noting that support teams must leverage AI."
cases.why: Detect-only mode, paraphrased, never saying 'AI-isms'.

cases.prompt: Fix the typos in this: "The meetign got moved to Thrusday at 3."
cases.why: Prose editing with no AI angle. The description states no boundary and the global CLAUDE.md loads a writing-style rule into every session, so over-firing on any edit is the likely failure.

cases.prompt: Create a podcast about the Salesforce flow inventory in NotebookLM.
cases.why: The claimed 'create a podcast about X'.

cases.prompt: Summarize this week's Hard Fork episode for me.
cases.why: Podcast-shaped, but consuming one rather than generating it. Third-party description with no boundary.

cases.prompt: Hand the search for every file that imports evalkit to a Haiku worker.
cases.why: A broad file search, first on Haiku's list, with the worker named.

cases.prompt: Have a Sonnet worker harvest the kit prices from Prairie Moon's pollinator power pack pages into a table.
cases.why: Harvesting sources into a table is on Sonnet's list. Read-only on purpose: these skills fork a real worker when they dispatch.

cases.prompt: Give this to a cheaper model: a first-pass summary of the 40-page energy audit PDF.
cases.why: The Haiku-vs-Sonnet boundary. No model named; first-pass summaries appear only on Sonnet's list. downshift-haiku is the failure.

cases.prompt: This migration is going to run long and I'll probably /clear halfway through. Keep the plan and findings on disk so we don't lose them.
cases.why: Surviving a /clear with plans on disk is the skill's whole pitch, without naming task_plan.md.

cases.prompt: Rename the variable cnt to count in run.py.
cases.why: Renames are on Haiku's list and the router rule is loaded in every dispatch, but a one-line rename is under its size floor. Catches the router over-firing.

cases.prompt: Should my scheduled tasks run on Haiku or Sonnet?
cases.why: Names both worker models but asks for advice. claude-api firing scores as outside tested set, same as mb-03.

cases.prompt: mine toil from my last month of Claude sessions
cases.why: Verbatim trigger for toil-mining, which sets disable-model-invocation: true. A dispatch to it scores as a miss, meaning the flag stopped being honored.

traps.label: car-check: purchase intent vs. automotive trivia
improvement-notes vs. interview debrief (disclaimed in its own description)
jira-ticket-builder: ticket request vs. case reporting (no stated boundary)
model-baseline: run the suite vs. opine on models (no stated boundary)
interview-loop: interview questions vs. plain scheduling
skill-check: health check vs. model baseline vs. skill discovery
garden-bed-build: new perennial bed vs. vegetable beds, one plant, and hardscape
flow-spec-builder: design a flow vs. debug one vs. ticket it
phonelog-channel: wiring PhoneLog vs. generic Discord questions
ship-sunday: the weekly increment vs. a one-off publish (no stated boundary)
advise-project-approach: project direction vs. a narrow bug
avoid-ai-writing: AI-tell audit vs. ordinary editing (no stated boundary)
notebooklm: generate in NotebookLM vs. consume a podcast
downshift-haiku / downshift-sonnet / planning-with-files vs. the router rule over-firing
